plan.dataFlow: A daily schedule job fetches all orders from the external commerce platform for the target period in bulk and writes pre-aggregated daily snapshots covering revenue totals, per-product sales figures, and per-customer order activity. When the merchant opens the admin dashboard and selects a date range, the app reads the relevant snapshot rows, computes aggregate revenue, AOV, top products, and repeat customer rate entirely from stored snapshots, and returns all four metrics in a single response. Because every metric is served from pre-aggregated tables, page load time is independent of total order volume. Orders with no associated customer are counted toward revenue and product snapshots but excluded from repeat customer rate calculations; zero-revenue orders are counted toward order volume but contribute nothing to revenue or AOV.

triggers.cadence: once daily during a low-traffic window
triggers.jobPurpose: Recompute and persist pre-aggregated daily metric snapshots so the admin dashboard can serve all four metrics instantly for any date range.
triggers.perTickWork: One tick fetches all orders placed on the previous calendar day in bulk, then writes or replaces the corresponding daily revenue snapshot row, daily per-product snapshot rows, and daily per-customer activity rows for that date.

edgeCases: A snapshot run is triggered a second time for the same target date before the first run completes — the second invocation must detect the in-progress run record and exit without writing any snapshot rows.
An order has no identifiable customer — it must be included in revenue and product snapshots but silently excluded from daily customer activity rows so repeat customer rate is not distorted.

All orders on a given day have zero revenue (e.g. fully discounted) — the daily revenue snapshot must still be written with zero revenue and the correct order count so AOV computes as zero rather than being absent from the range.

The merchant requests a date range that extends beyond the most recent completed snapshot date — the response must reflect the latest available data date so the merchant knows the figures are partial.

A product is deleted from the external platform after its snapshot rows have been written — historical product name and revenue figures must remain readable from the snapshot without requiring a live product lookup.

The daily job fails mid-run after writing the revenue snapshot but before writing product or customer snapshots — the run must be marked failed, the partial snapshot rows must not be served to the dashboard, and the next scheduled run must overwrite them cleanly.

hld_v_findings.issue: "single row looked up by target date to check whether a run for that day already completed before starting work" — the query pattern checks only for a *completed* run, but edge case 1 requires that an *in-progress* run also blocks a second invocation. The LLD will generate a guard query that filters on completed status only, meaning two concurrent schedule firings would both pass the check, proceed past the lock, and double-write all snapshot tables for the same date.
hld_v_findings.fix: Expand the query pattern to: "single row looked up by target date where status is in-progress or completed, to block any duplicate or concurrent invocation before any snapshot write occurs".

hld_v_findings.issue: "one row per scheduled run attempt, deduplicated by target date to prevent double-processing the same calendar day" — the phrase 'deduplicated by target date' signals a unique constraint on target date. Edge case 6 requires that after a failed run the next scheduled run must be able to write a new started record for the same date. A unique constraint blocks that INSERT, so the retry path described in edge case 6 is unbuildable without an explicit upsert or update-existing-failed-row strategy that the plan never declares.
hld_v_findings.fix: Change keyedBy to: "one row per run attempt; at most one non-failed row per target date — failed rows may be superseded by a subsequent attempt for the same date" and add a query pattern covering the update-on-retry access pattern, so the LLD plans an upsert rather than a plain INSERT with unique constraint.

daily-snapshot-job.description: Fetch all orders placed on the previous calendar day in bulk, then write or replace daily revenue, product, and customer-activity snapshot rows atomically; duplicate and concurrent runs are blocked by a workflow-guarded snapshot_runs row.

steps.purpose: Derive the target date as midnight UTC of the previous calendar day
steps.expression: (() => { const d = new Date(); d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() - 1); d.setUTCHours(0,0,0,0); return d.toISOString(); })()

steps.purpose: Derive the exclusive upper bound (midnight UTC of the current day) for the Shopify query filter
steps.expression: (() => { const d = new Date(); d.setUTCHours(0,0,0,0); return d.toISOString(); })()

steps.purpose: Check for an existing in-progress or completed run for the target date to prevent duplicate execution
steps.template: SELECT id, status FROM snapshot_runs WHERE target_date = ${targetDate} AND status IN ('running','completed') LIMIT 1

steps.purpose: Exit early if a concurrent or already-completed run exists for this target date

ifTrue.purpose: Warn operators that the run was skipped due to an existing active/completed run
ifTrue.message: snapshot run skipped: existing run detected

ifTrue.purpose: Abort without writing any snapshot rows

steps.purpose: Check for an existing failed run for the target date that should be reused (overwritten in place) rather than inserting a fresh row
steps.template: SELECT id FROM snapshot_runs WHERE target_date = ${targetDate} AND status = 'failed' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1

steps.purpose: Either reuse the existing failed run row or insert a new pending row

ifTrue.purpose: Reset the failed run row to pending so the workflow helper can claim it
ifTrue.template: UPDATE snapshot_runs SET status='pending', failure_reason=NULL, started_at=now(), completed_at=NULL WHERE id=${runId}

ifTrue.purpose: Capture the reused run id for downstream use

ifFalse.purpose: Insert a new pending snapshot_runs row for this target date
ifFalse.template: INSERT INTO snapshot_runs (target_date, status) VALUES (${targetDate}, 'pending') RETURNING id

ifFalse.purpose: Capture the new run id for downstream use

steps.purpose: Claim the pending run and execute all snapshot writes within the workflow lifecycle; failure_reason is persisted automatically on throw
steps.expression: await workflow.attempt('snapshot_runs', runId, { from: 'pending', to: 'running' }, async (row) => { const queryStr = `created_at:>=${targetDateIso} created_at:<${nextDayIso}`; const orders = []; for await (const node of shopify.graphqlPaginate(`query FetchOrders($cursor: String) { orders(first: 250, after: $cursor, query: "${queryStr}") { edges { cursor node { id totalPriceSet { shopMoney { amount currencyCode } } customer { id } lineItems(first: 50) { edges { node { quantity product { id title } originalTotalSet { shopMoney { amount currencyCode } } } } } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }`, {})) { orders.push(node); } const revenueRows = []; const productMap = new Map(); const customerMap = new Map(); let orderCount = 0; let zeroRevenueCount = 0; let currencyCode = 'USD'; for (const order of orders) { orderCount++; const shopMoney = order.totalPriceSet?.shopMoney; const rawAmount = shopMoney?.amount ?? '0'; const cc = shopMoney?.currencyCode ?? 'USD'; currencyCode = cc; const minorUnits = money.toMinorUnits(rawAmount, cc); if (minorUnits === 0) zeroRevenueCount++; revenueRows.push(minorUnits); const rawOrderId = Number(order.id.split('/').pop()); const customerId = order.customer?.id ? Number(order.customer.id.split('/').pop()) : null; if (customerId !== null) { customerMap.set(String(customerId), (customerMap.get(String(customerId)) ?? 0) + 1); } for (const liEdge of (order.lineItems?.edges ?? [])) { const li = liEdge.node; const prod = li.product; if (!prod) continue; const prodIdRaw = Number(prod.id.split('/').pop()); const prodKey = String(prodIdRaw); const liMoney = li.originalTotalSet?.shopMoney; const liMinor = liMoney ? money.toMinorUnits(liMoney.amount, liMoney.currencyCode ?? cc) : 0; const existing = productMap.get(prodKey); if (existing) { existing.units += li.quantity; existing.revenue = money.sum([existing.revenue, liMinor]); } else { productMap.set(prodKey, { product_external_id: prodIdRaw, product_name: prod.title ?? 'Unknown', units: li.quantity, revenue: liMinor, currency_code: liMoney?.currencyCode ?? cc }); } } } const totalRevenue = money.sum(revenueRows); await sql`INSERT INTO daily_revenue_snapshots (snapshot_date, currency_code, total_revenue, order_count, zero_revenue_order_count, updated_at) VALUES (${targetDateIso}, ${currencyCode}, ${totalRevenue}, ${orderCount}, ${zeroRevenueCount}, now()) ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE SET currency_code=EXCLUDED.currency_code, total_revenue=EXCLUDED.total_revenue, order_count=EXCLUDED.order_count, zero_revenue_order_count=EXCLUDED.zero_revenue_order_count, updated_at=now()`; await sql`DELETE FROM daily_product_snapshots WHERE snapshot_date=${targetDateIso}`; for (const [, p] of productMap) { await sql`INSERT INTO daily_product_snapshots (snapshot_date, product_external_id, product_name, currency_code, units_sold, revenue_contribution, updated_at) VALUES (${targetDateIso}, ${p.product_external_id}, ${p.product_name}, ${p.currency_code}, ${p.units}, ${p.revenue}, now()) ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date, product_external_id) DO UPDATE SET product_name=EXCLUDED.product_name, currency_code=EXCLUDED.currency_code, units_sold=EXCLUDED.units_sold, revenue_contribution=EXCLUDED.revenue_contribution, updated_at=now()`; } await sql`DELETE FROM daily_customer_activity WHERE snapshot_date=${targetDateIso}`; for (const [custIdStr, cnt] of customerMap) { await sql`INSERT INTO daily_customer_activity (snapshot_date, customer_external_id, orders_placed, updated_at) VALUES (${targetDateIso}, ${BigInt(custIdStr)}, ${cnt}, now()) ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date, customer_external_id) DO UPDATE SET orders_placed=EXCLUDED.orders_placed, updated_at=now()`; } })

steps.purpose: Record successful completion of the snapshot run for operational monitoring

postconditions: Exactly one daily_revenue_snapshots row exists for target_date after the run
One daily_product_snapshots row exists per distinct product seen in the day's orders
One daily_customer_activity row exists per distinct identifiable customer seen in the day's orders
snapshot_runs row for this run has status='completed' and completed_at is set

edgeCases: If target_date already has status='running' or 'completed' in snapshot_runs, the recipe exits before writing any snapshot rows.
A prior failed run for target_date is detected and its row is reset to pending rather than inserting a new row, ensuring at most one run row per date per outcome.
Orders with no customer (guest checkout) are skipped for daily_customer_activity but included in revenue and product aggregations.
All orders have zero revenue — daily_revenue_snapshots row is still written with total_revenue=0 and order_count correct.
A product with no product node on a line item is skipped for daily_product_snapshots.

If the workflow callback throws mid-execution (e.g. after revenue write but before product writes), workflow.fail captures the error, status is set to failed, and the next scheduled run resets and retries from scratch, overwriting any partial product rows.

steps.purpose: Compute total revenue in minor units by summing all revenue rows

platformGaps.gap: Shopify's bulk order fetch returns a potentially large volume of orders requiring full pagination; there is no single-call aggregate endpoint for revenue or product totals.
platformGaps.mitigation: shopify.graphqlPaginate iterates the orders connection with cursor pagination inside the cron job, collecting all nodes before aggregation writes begin; per-item Shopify calls inside the loop are avoided.

platformGaps.gap: Shopify does not expose a batch mutation for inserting pre-aggregated snapshot rows; product and customer rows must be written per-item in the workflow callback.
platformGaps.mitigation: Snapshot writes are plain SQL upserts inside the workflow.attempt callback, which runs server-side without Shopify rate-limit exposure; only the read phase uses the Shopify API.

platformGaps.gap: The admin dashboard can only reflect data through the most recently completed snapshot date; orders placed after that date are not visible until the next cron tick.
platformGaps.mitigation: The response includes data_through_date so the merchant UI can display a clear 'data as of <date>' notice rather than implying real-time accuracy.
platformGaps.uxImplication: Admin dashboard should display a 'Data as of <date>' label alongside all metrics so the merchant understands the figures reflect the last completed daily snapshot, not live orders.

uxExpectations.admin: The admin dashboard should render all four metrics immediately on page load using the stored date range default from settings, with a visible 'Data as of <date>' label; the settings page should show current defaults pre-filled and save with a single button click.

edgeCases: A second cron invocation fires for the same target_date while the first is still running — the status='running' guard in snapshot_runs causes the second invocation to log and exit before touching any snapshot tables.

The daily job fails after writing daily_revenue_snapshots but before writing daily_product_snapshots — snapshot_runs.status is set to 'failed' by workflow.fail; the next run detects the failed row, resets it to pending, and overwrites all partial snapshot rows with fresh data.

A merchant queries a date range that extends past the most recent completed snapshot_date — data_through_date in the response reflects the latest actual snapshot, and the UI can surface a 'partial date range' notice.

A product is deleted from Shopify after its daily_product_snapshots rows have been written — the stored product_name column provides the display name for historical top-products queries without any live Shopify lookup.

All orders on a given day have zero revenue (fully discounted) — the daily_revenue_snapshots row is still written with total_revenue=0 and the correct order_count so AOV computes correctly as zero rather than being absent from the range.

On first install before any cron tick has completed, the admin dashboard receives empty snapshot tables and returns zeroed metrics with data_through_date=null — the UI must handle null gracefully with a 'No data yet' state.
